title: Season 2, Ep 3: Multi-tenant platform architecture
oneliner: One centralized AI platform for all business units - with hard tenant isolation so each LOB only reaches its own area, and usage metering so each pays for what it uses.
says: Enterprises have multiple LOBs building AI projects, and you cannot give each its own platform - that is a cost overhead. You need one centralized AI platform for all LOBs. Two design requirements: hard tenant isolation so each LOB accesses only its own area of the platform, and usage metering for each LOB.
explained: This episode is the season's economic spine (the core economic idea the season is built on). One platform per LOB multiplies everything - cost, headcount, security surface. One shared platform divides cost but creates the two problems he names. Isolation answers the trust problem: LOB A's data, prompts, and agent runs must be unreachable by LOB B, enforced by the platform rather than by policy documents. 'Hard' isolation means the boundary is technical - separate namespaces, keys, quotas - not a promise.

Metering answers the fairness problem and enables something subtler: accountability creates optimization pressure. When each LOB sees its token consumption and cost, the inference-economy discipline from Season 1 becomes self-enforcing - teams cache, route to smaller models, and clean up idle agents because the bill has their name on it (each unit is billed for its own usage). Isolation plus metering is what turns 'shared platform' from a cost dump (a shared expense nobody manages) into a product.
takeaway: Shared platform economics work only with hard tenant isolation and per-tenant metering - trust and cost, both enforced by the platform itself.
